title: The bubble machine

predict.q: Buyers start to expect house prices to rise 10% next year. What happens to the market **now**?

options.s: Demand falls, because homes already look expensive.
options.fb: That treats a price change as a cause of lower demand. Expectations of higher prices are a reason to buy now: they shift demand right.

options.s: Supply shifts right, because sellers expect higher prices.
options.fb: Sellers expecting higher prices may hold back homes, if anything reducing supply now. The big move here is in demand.

options.s: Demand shifts right, so the price rises today.
options.fb: Buyers rush to buy before prices rise: D1 shifts to D2 and the price index rises from 200 to 266.7 now.

options.s: Nothing changes until prices actually rise next year.
options.fb: Expectations act today: buyers rush to buy before prices rise, so demand shifts now.

task: Move the **Expected price change** slider from 0 to +10% and watch D1 move to D2. Then add **Feedback rounds**, and try −10%.

target.do: Move the Expected price change slider to +10% (feedback rounds 0), then press Check.

takeaway: Expectations shift demand, so beliefs about prices can push prices up, and then down, with no change in the homes themselves.
explore: Add feedback rounds (price 300, then 316.7), then set −10% and add rounds again.
